result:
I'd make people a little better at disagreeing well: more willing to consider they might be wrong, more curious about why someone sees things differently, less likely to treat disagreement as a sign the other person is stupid or malicious.

It might seem like an odd pick over something concrete like ending disease or poverty. But many of our biggest problems aren't stuck because nobody knows what to do. They're stuck because people can't coordinate, trust each other, or update when evidence changes. If that improved even modestly, it would make almost every other problem more solvable, including ones I can't anticipate. It's a lever on everything else.

It also appeals to me because it doesn't require imposing any particular vision of the good life. A world where people reason together better can still be a world of wildly different values and choices. It just gets better at working through the conflicts.

I'm wary of "one change" wishes in general. Directly fixing a single outcome can have strange side effects, while improving how people think and cooperate seems more robust.

What about you? Is there something you'd change?
